categories.main_business_segments: NextEra Energy, Inc. (NEE) operates two principal business segments: Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), a rate-regulated electric utility serving Florida, and NextEra Energy Resources (NEER), which includes competitive energy and rate-regulated transmission businesses focused on clean energy generation and infrastructure across North America.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FPL's operations are based on large-scale electric generation, transmission, and distribution, utilizing a diverse mix of natural gas, solar, nuclear, and some coal generation, with significant investments in battery storage. NEER is a global leader in wind and solar generation, battery storage, and also operates natural gas pipelines and transmission assets, leveraging advanced renewable technologies and large-scale project development expertise.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FPL primarily serves residential, commercial, and industrial customers in Florida, with over 5.8 million customer accounts. NEER sells energy, capacity, and related products mainly to wholesale customers such as utilities, municipalities, and cooperatives across the U.S. and Canada, and also provides full energy and capacity requirements, risk management, and trading services.
categories.geographic_coverage: FPL operates throughout most of the east and lower west coasts of Florida and in eight counties in northwest Florida. NEER operates in 40 U.S. states and 4 Canadian provinces, with generation and transmission assets distributed across North America, and a focus on regions with strong renewable resource potential.
categories.supply_chain_position: FPL operates as a vertically integrated, downstream utility, managing generation, transmission, and distribution to end customers. NEER is primarily a power producer (IPP) and transmission owner, positioned midstream to downstream, selling power and capacity to wholesale customers and utilities, and also participates in upstream gas infrastructure through pipeline ownership.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: NEE's strategic priorities center on expanding clean energy leadership, investing in renewable generation, battery storage, and grid modernization, while maintaining low customer bills and high reliability. The company is focused on leveraging policy incentives, scaling solar and wind, developing green hydrogen and renewable fuels, and pursuing innovation in energy storage and transmission technologies.
categories.revenue_model: FPL generates revenue primarily through regulated electricity sales to retail and wholesale customers, with rates set by regulatory bodies. NEER earns revenue from long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs), energy and capacity sales, renewable energy credits, transmission tariffs, and commodity trading, with a significant portion under long-term contracts providing stable cash flows.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FPL faces limited direct competition in its regulated Florida market but competes with self-generation and alternative energy providers. NEER competes with other independent power producers and utilities in the wholesale market, but is the world's largest generator of wind and solar energy, positioning itself as a clean energy leader with scale, execution capability, and financial strength.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: NEE is one of the largest electric power and energy infrastructure companies in North America, with 2022 operating revenues of $21.0 billion and net income attributable to NEE of $4.1 billion. The company has demonstrated strong, sustained growth, with a five-year total shareholder return of 139.3%, and continues to invest heavily in renewable and grid infrastructure, supporting a robust growth trajectory.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: NEE emphasizes a value proposition of low customer bills, high reliability, outstanding customer service, and clean energy. Its competitive differentiation lies in its scale and expertise in renewables, industry-leading cost structure, ability to deliver long-term contracted cash flows, and a proven track record of innovation and execution in clean energy and grid modernization.
